Document 1

Spy School — 3 steps

Work through the document in the same order as in class.

1. Describe the poster

This is a poster for the British TV show Spy School. In the foreground, we can see two adults dressed like secret agents. The poster suggests that young contestants will train to become spies.

2. Present the document

Nature: a poster for a TV programme.
Title: Spy School.
Source: CITV / UKGameshows.
Topic: a spy-training show for children.

Model: This document is a poster for a British TV show called Spy School. It presents a programme in which young contestants learn how to become spies.
Method: nature of the document → title → source → topic / main idea.

3. Understand the text

Two children train as spies and develop physical and problem-solving skills. They learn to solve puzzles and break codes. Guided by a spy handler, they complete missions around London. Their final objective is to stop Goldfist, an evil mastermind.
Document 2

The Recruit

1. Describe the book cover

This is the book cover of The Recruit by Robert Muchamore. In the foreground, a teenage boy is climbing down a rope. The orange and black colours and the action scene create a dangerous, exciting atmosphere. The title and the CHERUB logo suggest a story about young secret agents.

2. Understand the text

CHERUB agents are highly trained and very talented. They are sent on missions to spy on criminals, terrorists and drug dealers. Because they are teenagers, adults do not suspect them. James is the latest CHERUB recruit, but before going into the field, he must survive very difficult basic training.
Grammar

What you need to know

The superlative

short adjective → the + adj-est
strong → the strongest
quick → the quickest
long adjective → the most + adjective
talented → the most talented
irregular: good → the best

Use the superlative to compare one person or thing with the rest of a group.

Expressing capacity

can / can't + verb
She can break codes.
be able to + verb
He is able to go undercover.
be capable of + V-ing
They are capable of solving puzzles.
be good at + V-ing
She is good at deciphering codes.
master + noun / V-ing
He has mastered skiing.
